results.query: I cloned CyberSand on Windows. Must I have C:/kybersand and dev.cmd before I can open the Workbench?
results.bounded_context_answer: No. A source-only checkout supplies launch-desktop.cmd; dev.cmd and C:/kybersand belong to the separate companion workspace. Materialize the runtime and use the exact pinned Godot. Launch the project through its checked wrapper and choose the Workbench.
context_notes: Correct answer at ranks1/5, but rank4 captured an interim invalid extra-argument example for launch-desktop.cmd. The PowerShell wrapper accepts only Godot, Editor and PrintIdentityOnly, so do not copy that command. Source page corrected after this snapshot.
Web/physics companion instructions in ranks2/3 are out of scope for first desktop launch.

results.query: How do I paint, erase, fill and undo in a first Workbench session?
results.bounded_context_answer: Open the Workbench, pause, choose Paint and use Brush(B), Eraser(E/right-drag), Fill(G) and Ctrl+Z Undo. Precise shapes, Fill and history need paused state; focused text fields retain keys. Wait for native completion and stop/settle active Art before shared Undo. Simulation invalidates unsafe construction history.
context_notes: Rank2 carries old Draft/candidate metadata although the tool/control text is accepted current behavior. This metadata was corrected after the saved snapshot.

results.query: An Art batch returned queued=true. May I say the cells have been applied and displayed?
results.bounded_context_answer: No. queued is admission; executing means a worker has claimed a chunk. Wait for actual native receipts to report changed/unchanged/excluded/refused cells and any partial prefix. Neither queued nor a native applied count alone proves that a presented frame displayed the result.
context_notes: Current question answered directly at rank1. Ranks2/4 contain unrelated dated inference material and stale unmerged metadata. Rank5 names obsolete history_result rather than current native_history_action; corrected contract removes this contamination.

results.query: Does ordinary Save restore the exact next tick, moving actors, solver queues and private Art conversation?
results.bounded_context_answer: No. Ordinary Save is an authored-start reconstruction, not a complete evolved physical checkpoint. The provided contexts explicitly exclude last-tick continuation and restored Undo/Art session history; Art begins empty in a new game session. They do not give the full serialized-field inventory, so exact queue/actor-state details should be checked in the save contract.

results.query: Does hiding the Art window mean its request was stopped?
results.bounded_context_answer: No. Closing the Art window hides it and keeps the Workbench session. Use Stop to cancel HTTP/capture and future turns and request native retirement; an executing slice may finish and report partial changed cells. Wait for receipts and other authoring work to settle before history actions.
context_notes: Rank2 directly answers. Historical scanline results and linked-segment export wording in lower-ranked provider excerpts are unrelated/obsolete and must not be generalized. They are reconciled in the current file.

results.query: After accepted ART-SESSION-LOG-001, are yesterday’s Art conversation messages automatically restored on the next game launch?
results.bounded_context_answer: No. Every new Workbench session starts with an empty Art conversation. Hiding/reopening within the same session keeps it, but new Send does not attach old archives. Nonsecret preferences may persist; older logs remain on disk for deliberate diagnosis.
context_notes: Rank1 stale unmerged scope conflicts with acceptance wording, but current session-only behavior is explicit and corroborated by ranks2/4. Metadata now corrected.

results.query: Which Art diagnostics can I attach to a public bug report without leaking prompts or credentials?
results.bounded_context_answer: Attach a minimal synthetic reproduction with source/runtime identity, platform, steps, expected/actual result and a manually inspected/redacted error or receipt extract. Do not attach entire Art archives by default. Automatic credential redaction does not make prompts, model replies, images or arbitrary private text safe to publish.
context_notes: No retrieved source grants blanket safety to raw/exported JSONL. Rank2 linked-segment details are stale but do not change the privacy warning.

results.query: Can I paint all four Strata Theatre planes in the ordinary Shared Workbench on main?
results.bounded_context_answer: No. Accepted Strata Theatre is a separate opt-in layered host; ordinary Workbench integration is a candidate. In the standalone host, the background remains immutable even if selected as a paint target. Its controls and layered presentation do not grant four-plane Workbench authoring.
context_notes: Top result is standalone controls, but its scope plus rank4 explicitly preserve the ordinary-Workbench boundary.

results.query: Are persistent areas, RAMCACHE and exact off-screen catch-up already part of ordinary accepted Workbench saves?
results.bounded_context_answer: No. Persistent areas and bounded game-time catch-up are approved direction and separately scoped unmerged work. Current interest-region re-entry restores eligibility rather than elapsed-time catch-up; ordinary authored saves do not include a residency/cache manager or exact off-screen continuation.
context_notes: The answer preserves approved intent instead of treating current absence as permanent rejection. Do not substitute real-world offline elapsed time for game time.

results.query: Can I use the World Art viewer and large PNG captures without treating its dimensions as native playable World capacity?
results.bounded_context_answer: Yes, within the standalone art adapter/export limits. Art input supports up to16384cells per side and16777216cells total; interactive full PNG uses50million output pixels, while explicit streamed capture allows100million and65536per output axis. These rendering limits do not qualify playable World size, physics, traversal or save/import compatibility.
